$comment: One price schedule — GitHub issue #366, DECISIONS.md § D525 clause 2, docs/38 § 2.1. Every price a player pays for a change, in one place, so the same change costs the same in Scenario, in Career and in the fix-a-building editor. The figures are DRAFTED, not measured: a price is game feel and the ladder's ordering is the product owner's. Where two shipped lists already agreed the agreed figure is kept and said so; where they disagreed the disagreement is recorded in the entry's note. See packages/viz/src/pricing/parse.ts. GitHub issue #467 (DECISIONS.md § D535) added two things. Six new rows and three paths added to dispatch-rules, at no change to its price, price the twenty-two dials the scenarios used to offer for nothing, and every note that carries them is an AGENT'S PROPOSAL, APPROVED AS DRAFTED by the product owner on 2026-09-11, saying field by field what is MEASURED (nothing about the figure), what is DERIVED (the ceiling the shipped opening budgets and stage hints put on it) and what is CHOSEN. And a `withheld` block names what no scenario sells at any price, by the product owner's own ruling: not for sale is a different answer from priced high, so it is a list of paths and a note rather than a row carrying a large number.

tiers.name: Dispatcher
tiers.note: How the cars are told to behave. Nothing is installed and nothing is cut, so it is the cheap end of the ladder and tuning is nearly free.

tiers.name: Equipment
tiers.note: Settings and fittings on kit the building already has — door timings, sensors, landing panels. Dearer than telling the cars what to do, cheaper than changing the building.

tiers.name: Building
tiers.note: The fabric: a new shaft or car, a faster or larger machine, a rezoned bank. The dearest end, and the only one that books long works.

changes.name: Where idle cars wait
changes.note: Free in every shipped list. Four fix cases price the idle strategy at 0 units and none prices it higher.

changes.name: How calls are assigned
changes.note: The fix cases price an assignment-mode change at 2 units as a diagnosis and at 8 as a costly fix. 2 is taken: the 8 was a case where the same press also bought a split threshold, which is priced on its own row now. GitHub issue #467 WIDENED WHAT THIS ROW COVERS AND DID NOT MOVE ITS PRICE: the three eligibility filters, the direction-reversal constraint and the sole-car bypass guard were free in every scenario that offered them, and they are bought here now. AGENT'S PROPOSAL, drafted for the product owner to accept, tighten or reject under the 2026-09-08 standing ruling on governed data/ values, and priced rather than withheld by the owner's 2026-09-10 ruling on that issue (DECISIONS.md § D535). APPROVED AS DRAFTED by the product owner on 2026-09-11. MEASURED: nothing about the figure, which is this row's unchanged 2 u; what is measured is only that buying this row reaches a run (packages/viz/src/scenario/pricedRowsReachTheRun.test.ts). DERIVED: that these five dials cannot sit on a row of their own. Stages 9 and 10 open on 15 u and suggest constraints.noDirectionReversal and answer.allowBypassIfSoleEligibleCar respectively beside dispatch.assignmentMode, weights.starvation and a landing-panel lever at 13 u, and packages/viz/src/campaign/parse.ts prices a stage's suggested levers together at its opening rung — measured by the loader on the first draft of this issue, which priced them on two 2 u rows of their own and was refused at 17 u against 15 on both stages. CHOSEN: this row rather than re-authoring two stages' hints or their opening rule, because the dials are part of the same act this row already sells — core declares the eligibility filters and the hard constraint in the stage of its dispatch pipeline that decides which cars a call may go to, and its own descriptions name opposite-direction pickup and no direction reversal as the two halves of conventional collective behaviour — and because the bypass guard is a starvation rule, as weights.starvation beside it is. Covered as groups where core groups them, so an eligibility filter or a hard constraint core declares tomorrow is priced here with no edit. FOR THE OWNER: the hints on stage-2-morning-rush, stage-7-prove-it, stage-8-the-headline-address, stage-10-the-bed-and-the-visitor and brief-e5-handling-capacity name answer.allowBypassIfSoleEligibleCar, a dial this row now sells, and on each of those scenarios moving it alone leaves every replication of both seed sets unchanged, so following that hint now costs 2 u for an unchanged run; packages/viz/src/scenario/pricedRowsReachTheRun.test.ts measures this and holds it in both directions as HINTS_THAT_DO_NOT_MOVE_THE_RUN, which an entry leaves only on the commit that makes its move change a replication.

changes.name: How long doors are told to hold
changes.note: Telling the controller when to close, as opposed to re-fitting the door. Priced at 2 and 4 in the two cases that buy it; 3 is the midpoint.

changes.name: When a call is handed to a car
changes.note: AGENT'S PROPOSAL — GitHub issue #467, drafted for the product owner to accept, tighten or reject under the 2026-09-08 standing ruling on governed data/ values, and priced rather than withheld by the owner's 2026-09-10 ruling on that issue (DECISIONS.md § D535). APPROVED AS DRAFTED by the product owner on 2026-09-11. MEASURED: nothing about the figure. No shipped list priced these dials — until this row every scenario that offered them offered them for nothing — so there is no agreed figure to keep and no disagreement to record. What is measured is only that the purchase reaches a run: packages/viz/src/scenario/pricedRowsReachTheRun.test.ts finds a shipped scenario whose opening budget buys it and whose legs it moves. DERIVED: the ceiling. No stage that opens on 4 u offers these dials, and the scenarios that do offer them open on 15 u, which packages/viz/src/scenario/budget.test.ts re-derives as the dearest dial they reach — destination-panels at 13 u — plus the dispatcher tier's typical of 2 u; so this row may cost up to 13 u before those budgets move. CHOSEN: 2 u, the dispatcher tier's typical. The window a deferred assignment waits and the window a call is held so near-simultaneous presses merge are both answers to one question — how long the controller waits before it decides — and dispatch.deferWindowS is live only when dispatch.assignmentTiming is deferred, so selling the window apart from the timing would sell a disabled control. That is the defect packages/viz/src/scenario/budgetReachesTheRun.test.ts found when a landing panel's call type was bought without its assignment.

changes.name: Let a call move to another car
changes.note: AGENT'S PROPOSAL — GitHub issue #467, drafted for the product owner to accept, tighten or reject under the 2026-09-08 standing ruling on governed data/ values, and priced rather than withheld by the owner's 2026-09-10 ruling on that issue (DECISIONS.md § D535). What is measured is only that the purchase reaches a run: packages/viz/src/scenario/pricedRowsReachTheRun.test.ts finds a shipped scenario whose opening budget buys it and whose legs it moves. DERIVED: the ceiling. Stages 2 and 3 open on 4 u and offer all four dials, and packages/viz/src/scenario/budget.test.ts re-derives every opening budget as the dearest dial a stage offers plus the dispatcher tier's typical of 2 u, so this row cannot cost more than 2 u without re-authoring those budgets. CHOSEN: 2 u, the dispatcher tier's typical. One row, because core gates the other three dials on dispatch.reassignmentPolicy — each is live only under a policy that lets a call move — and a hysteresis bought without the policy it tunes would be a disabled control sold at a price.

changes.name: How a wait and a distance are scaled before they are weighed
changes.note: AGENT'S PROPOSAL — GitHub issue #467, drafted for the product owner to accept, tighten or reject under the 2026-09-08 standing ruling on governed data/ values, and priced rather than withheld by the owner's 2026-09-10 ruling on that issue (DECISIONS.md § D535). APPROVED AS DRAFTED by the product owner on 2026-09-11. MEASURED: nothing about the figure. No shipped list priced these dials — until this row every scenario that offered them offered them for nothing — so there is no agreed figure to keep and no disagreement to record. What is measured is only that the purchase reaches a run: packages/viz/src/scenario/pricedRowsReachTheRun.test.ts finds a shipped scenario whose opening budget buys it and whose legs it moves. DERIVED: the ceiling. No stage that opens on 4 u offers these dials, and the scenarios that do offer them open on 15 u, which packages/viz/src/scenario/budget.test.ts re-derives as the dearest dial they reach — destination-panels at 13 u — plus the dispatcher tier's typical of 2 u; so this row may cost up to 13 u before those budgets move. CHOSEN: 2 u, the price dispatch-rules charges to re-tune the weights, because this re-tunes the curve those weights are applied to — core's description: it changes the curvature of the map rather than its gain, so no rescaled weight recovers it. Its own row rather than a path added to dispatch-rules: the paths this issue did add to that row are the five that shipped stage hints price beside it, which this curve is not. Worth knowing before buying it: core measures each of these dials inert on a profile with a single weighted term.

changes.name: When doors reopen, and how long boarding may hold them
changes.note: AGENT'S PROPOSAL — GitHub issue #467, drafted for the product owner to accept, tighten or reject under the 2026-09-08 standing ruling on governed data/ values, and priced rather than withheld by the owner's 2026-09-10 ruling on that issue (DECISIONS.md § D535). Dispatcher tier for dwell-policy's stated reason: nothing is re-fitted. One row, because the reopen budget bounds the reopening the late-arrival hold asks for, and the transfer ceiling bounds the same stop from the other side; core describes each as a bound on how long one stop can last.

One row, because core requires the overload threshold not to be below the bypass threshold, so the two are set together. The equipment tier's median is 9 u with this row in it, as it was without.

changes.name: Pressurise the cabins
changes.note: AGENT'S PROPOSAL — GitHub issue #444. A flat equipment row, which is what this issue's own body asks for and what the schedule already grants; #478's magnitude term is not needed and its block on this issue was mis-applied. MEASURED: nothing. No shipped list prices this change, because it did not exist before #444, so there is no agreed figure to keep and no disagreement to record — unlike every other row in this file. CHOSEN: 11 units and 2 nights. 11 sits between door-sensors (9 u, 1 night) and destination-panels (13 u, 2 nights), which is where the ladder puts it by kind: it is a fitting on kit the building already has — a pressure vessel and a bleed valve on an existing cabin — rather than a new machine or a new shaft, so it is above a sensor and below a landing-panel refit. 2 nights matches destination-panels, on the reasoning that a car is out of service while its cabin is worked on. Both figures are game feel and the ladder's ordering is the product owner's (see this file's own header). WHAT IT BUYS, and the reason it is not a dominant buy: it lifts the air-pressure descent cap in data/elevator-specs.json, which only binds a bank whose travel is above airPressure.appliesAboveTravelM and whose cars are rated faster than airPressure.descentCapMps. On every shipped building as built it buys exactly zero seconds, and the loader says so (pressurisation-buys-nothing). It becomes worth 11 units only after the player has bought speed the shaft cannot spend going down — which is the decision #444 exists to create.

changes.name: Fit regenerative drives
changes.note: AGENT'S PROPOSAL — GitHub issue #431, DECISIONS.md § D539. A flat equipment row, which is what the issue's own body asks for. MEASURED: nothing. No shipped list prices this change, because it did not exist before #431, so there is no agreed figure to keep. CHOSEN: 12 units and 2 nights. 12 sits between cabin-pressurisation (11 u) and destination-panels (13 u): it is a drive and inverter retrofit on machines the building already has, which is more than a fitting on an existing cabin and less than a landing-panel refit, and well under machines-4mps (14 u, building tier), which is new machines. 2 nights matches cabin-pressurisation, on the reasoning that a car is out of service while its drive is changed. Both figures are game feel, and the ladder's ordering is the product owner's (see this file's own header). WHAT IT BUYS, and the reason it is a decision rather than a dominant buy: energy only. It moves energyKJ, workPerServedLegKJ and the fifth goal's verdict and never a leg (§ D539), and how much it moves them depends on how much of a building's travel overhauls. Measured on a 28-run probe under collective at § D468's seeds, the whole-run saving is 6-14 % at midtown-office, 13-21 % at chancery-house and secure-tower, 24-34 % at crown-hotel, st-jude-hospital and mixed-use-high-rise, and 31-43 % at garden-apartments — against the 20-40 % band elevator-specs.json's regenerativeDrive block cites.

changes.name: Rebalance the counterweights
changes.note: AGENT'S PROPOSAL — GitHub issue #431, DECISIONS.md § D539. A flat equipment row. MEASURED: nothing; no shipped list prices it. CHOSEN: 3 units and 1 night. Adding or removing filler weights in a counterweight frame is docs/38 § 2.1's own description of the equipment tier — a setting on kit already installed — so it sits with the cheap end of that tier, between door-dwell (2 u) and faster-doors (4 u). 1 night because a car is taken out of service to be re-weighed. Both figures are game feel and the owner's. WHAT IT BUYS: energy only, like regenerative-drive. The ratio may be set anywhere in the cited 0.4-0.5 band (core config/schema.ts BANK_ENERGY_TUNABLES), and whether its best setting differs by traffic pattern is measured by benchmark/counterweightOptimum.ts rather than assumed; if it does not, the row is a dial that changes a number and not a decision, and the study says so.

changes.name: A faster machine
changes.note: THE CLEAREST CONFLICT THE SCHEDULE RESOLVES. The same purchase — make a machine faster — was priced three ways: the fix cases charge 8, 9 or 10 units for a 0.5 m/s bump and 12 for 1.0; `fixit/engine.ts#EDITOR_PRICING.speedUnitsPerHalfMps` charges 6; the campaign shop's machine tiers are 14, 25 and 40. A player paid a different price for the same metre per second depending on which screen they stood on. 10 is taken — the fix cases' mode — so the editor's step moves 6 to 10. The campaign shop's three machine tiers are re-specifications of the whole fleet to a named class and are separate rows below, on `larger-car-step`'s ground: widening one car and re-specifying the fleet are different acts.

withheld.note: RULED BY THE PRODUCT OWNER on 2026-09-10, on GitHub issue #467: 'Hide the advanced families, price the rest' — DECISIONS.md § D535. Not a price and not an agent's proposal. The issue that measured the gap named this family: the weight-set selector is the machinery Phase 6c refused three times (§ D145, § D156, and the re-measurement § D162 pre-registered), and offering it for sale is a different product claim from offering a fifth car. So no scenario offers a dial under dispatcher.selection at any rung: packages/viz/src/campaign/parse.ts#editableIdsOf resolves the whole group out of every scenario's editable set, and packages/viz/src/scenario/budget.ts#admitPurchase refuses a move that touches one. Withheld as a group, so a selector knob core declares tomorrow is withheld with no edit here. It carries no price, no tier and no nights because not for sale is a different answer from priced high. The Engineer parameter controls, which have no budget, still draw these dials.

RULED BY THE PRODUCT OWNER on 2026-09-10, on GitHub issue #467 — DECISIONS.md § D535, the same ruling as weight-set-selector's. Not a price and not an agent's proposal. The six tuning knobs of what core's predictor schema calls the learned arrival model. Withheld by exact path rather than as a group, because dispatcher.idle also holds the parking dials idle-parking prices: a predictor knob core declares tomorrow therefore arrives neither priced nor withheld, and packages/viz/src/scenario/budget.test.ts's register turns red until somebody decides which answer it gets. The predicted-demand parking strategy stays on sale under idle-parking: a scenario may park cars by the forecast and may not re-tune the forecaster. The Engineer parameter controls, which have no budget, still draw these dials.
